lesson_title: Splitting the Fare and Spreading the News: Hyperbolas and Exponentials
hook_text: Two things that can never happen in a taxi. Both of them are drawn on your graph.
clip_script: A trip costs a hundred and twenty rand, fixed, no matter how many people climb in. Two passengers? Sixty each. Three? Forty. Four? Thirty. Six? Twenty. Notice the drop — huge at first, then tiny. Going from two to three saves everyone twenty rand. Going from eleven to twelve saves less than a rand. Now the two things that can never happen. Squeeze in more and more people and the share keeps shrinking — but it never reaches zero. Somebody always pays something. And you can never split the fare among zero people. That's not a small number, it's not a thing at all. Those two impossibilities are the two lines your curve leans towards and never touches — asymptotes. And it's why this graph has no crossing on the vertical axis. Not a hard one to find. None. Now a different story. Someone tells one learner some news. First break, that learner tells two. Next break, each of those tells two more. One, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two — by the tenth round it's over a thousand. Boring, boring, boring, EXPLOSION. And run it backwards: half a teller, a quarter, an eighth — you can halve forever and always have something left. So that curve creeps along just above the bottom line and never lands. Same idea, opposite direction.
visual_style: A minibus taxi filling up as a rand-per-person figure drops and a hyperbola traces itself; then a school corridor where whispers branch two at a time while an exponential curve rockets up beside it.
mood: Street-smart, quick, a little dramatic on the explosion.
pacing: Rhythmic on the fare splits, a pause on 'zero people', accelerating hard through the doubling.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch both curves asymptote-first.
